question: InnoEnergy was awarded EUR 10 million in EU support for the training and reskilling of workers in the European battery sector1. The company subsequently announced that more than 100 000 people had been trained. A review shows, however, that the figure was based on certificates issued rather than on the number of individuals, meaning that one person could be counted several times over.
Certificates could be obtained even with a score of 0 % in a test, and around 10 % of the reported participants came from a Minecraft-based educational game aimed at children2.

Although InnoEnergy is currently being investigated by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office for suspected grant and VAT fraud, the EU has already granted an additional EUR 9 million to InnoEnergy to set up a similar academy for the solar energy sector3. With the above in mind: 1.
Why has InnoEnergy been awarded additional grants despite ongoing investigations into grant and VAT fraud?
Why has InnoEnergy been awarded additional grants despite the extensive accounting shortcomings described above?
Will the Commission seek recovery of the funds concerned if it finds that EU grants have been misused, and will additional EU funding be suspended?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.11.2026) The Commission takes any allegation of irregularity or misuse of EU funds seriously and takes all measures to protect the EU budget.

The Commission cannot comment on ongoing investigations carried out by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office as it is an independent EU body responsible for investigating and prosecuting criminal offences affecting the EU’s financial interests. Such investigations are subject to applicable confidentiality requirements and procedural safeguards.

Funding for the European Battery Alliance Academy is based on contractual relations between InnoEnergy and the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT). The EIT, an EU body with an independent management board, is currently assessing the final report. The Commission expects all EU-funded actions to meet high standards of sound financial management, transparency and credibility.

If shortcomings, irregularities or misuse of EU funds are confirmed, the Commission takes the appropriate measures in line with the Financial Regulation1 and the relevant grant agreements, including possible grant suspension, termination or recovery of funds and exclusion of entities from further EU funding.
